target_question: Does the self-reported pattern resemble a symptomatic human prion-disease syndrome requiring escalation?

scope: use this screening as the first Simptomat calibration case
store a pseudonymized machine-readable record in the public Simptomat repository
duplicate a research-state mirror in the JANUS meta-registry
consent.public_git_warning: Public Git history can be copied or retained. Withdrawal can stop future use and remove current-branch content, but cannot guarantee erasure from every clone, cache, or historical object.

screening_questions.note: No positive progression signal established.
Held unresolved; not converted to yes/no.
No new balance/coordination decline reported; coin-catching anecdote is not a validated neurological test.
Only goosebumps/piloerection reported; not classified as myoclonus.
No new visual syndrome reported.
No forced classification.
No functional decline reported.
An isolated unilateral thigh numbness episode was reported; retained as a separate peripheral-nerve hypothesis rather than a prion-positive signal.
No motor weakness reported.
At least one episodic forgetting phenomenon endorsed; exact subtype not specified.
No clear increase in frequency or severity over 3-6 months.
No known CJD/FFI/GSS/pathogenic-PRNP family history reported.
No neurosurgery/spinal surgery, corneal transplant, dura mater graft, or human pituitary-derived growth hormone reported.
Longstanding irregular sleep schedule makes this item uninterpretable.
Change endorsed.
Change described as non-deteriorating and subjectively constructive, with preserved adult control.
No new rigidity, tremor, bradykinesia, dystonia/spasm, or involuntary movement syndrome reported.
Ordinary intention-forgetting reported without recurrent disorientation pattern.
No new motor-speech decline reported.
No loss of ability in everyday complex tasks reported.
No personal residence/long stay during the main BSE exposure era reported.
No prolonged personal stay reported.
Plasma transfusion in childhood reported; stored as exposure history, not evidence of prion infection.
No psychiatric-to-neurological progression sequence reported.
No sudden confusion with simple-task impairment or post-event amnesia reported.
No handwriting/fine-motor deterioration reported.
Intermittent skipped-beat sensation mentioned; insufficient to classify as a new autonomic syndrome.
Sensation reported since childhood, stable, and without syncope, severe dizziness, chest pain/pressure, or marked dyspnea.
No decline reported; participant reports subjective improvement in associative reasoning.
Short/irregular sleep without fatigue described as longstanding rather than a new state.
No new impulsive/risk-taking syndrome reported.
Participant reports deliberate verification, counterexample checking, and willingness to revise conclusions.
Fast/loud speech and associative topic transitions described as longstanding baseline traits, not new progression.

ambiguous_or_non_specific_items: isolated thigh sensory symptom without weakness

result.what_this_supports: The self-reported answers did not assemble the typical rapidly progressive symptomatic syndrome that would ordinarily raise concern for CJD/vCJD.
what_this_does_not_support: It does not prove absence of prions.
It does not exclude presymptomatic/incubating prion disease.
It does not diagnose another condition.
It does not replace neurological examination, MRI, EEG, CSF testing, genetics, or clinician judgment.
It does not establish sensitivity, specificity, predictive value, calibration, or clinical utility for Simptomat.

escalation_gate.trigger: New rapidly progressive decline over weeks to months, especially cognition plus coordination/myoclonus/vision/speech/movement loss, or other acute neurological red flags.
possible_clinical_tools_when_indicated: CSF RT-QuIC and other clinician-selected tests

forbidden_use: training a model to output clinical diagnoses without external labels
treating repeated self-reports as physician-confirmed outcomes
calibration_use.future_calibration_requirement: Diagnostic-performance calibration requires consented cases with independently established clinical reference labels and an appropriate study design; repeated self-report cases alone are insufficient.

references.topic: Human prion disease surveillance and testing

provenance.normalization_rule: Free-text answers were converted conservatively; uncertainty remained uncertainty and longstanding baseline traits were not promoted to new progressive symptoms.
